raw_graphql_pull_request.body: - [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR. # What does this PR do? ### Description This PR fixes several numerical semantics in the multi-head HyperConnection (mHC) module to align with the reference implementation of DeepSeek-V4 (Ref: [DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/inference](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/tree/main/inference)), while keeping the existing BF16 storage/compute strategy for activations. **Changes:** 1. **Residual mixing orientation**: Removed the manual `comb.transpose(-1, -2)` since the fused kernel already applies `comb.T` internally. 2. **RMS normalization formula**: Fixed from `1 / (norm / sqrt(n) + eps)` to `torch.rsqrt(mean(square) + eps)`, adjusting the epsilon placement. 3. **Sinkhorn pre-epsilon**: Added `eps` to the `pre` output in `split_sinkhorn` to match the reference. 4. **Unit Tests**: Updated related unit tests with independent references and gradient checks. ### Why this is needed Before this fix, the mismatch in the residual mixing orientation (`transpose`) and epsilon placements led to significant performance degradation and training instability, especially when loading official checkpoints or running RL/SFT tasks. **1. RL Training Improvements** In our RL rollout vs. training evaluation, the Log PPL difference dropped dramatically after the fix. As shown below, the bug caused a severe mismatch (~0.10 diff), whereas the aligned implementation maintains near-zero difference (~0.0004 diff). **2. SFT Training & Evaluation Mismatch** During SFT training, the buggy implementation forced the model to compensate for the incorrect routing, resulting in an initially bloated loss (2.29 vs 1.29) and a massive gap in evaluation Log PPL when deployed on a correct vLLM instance. After the fix, the training loss and the vLLM evaluation Log PPL align perfectly from the start. :warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact `@NVIDIA/mcore-oncall`. ## Issue tracking For PRs from open-source community contributors: - **New features**: a linked issue is **required**. Please open a [feature request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) and reference it here before submitting the PR. - **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process. Linked issue: ## Contribution process ### Pre-checks - [ ] I have added relevant unit tests - [ ] I have added relevant functional tests - [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md)) - [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html) - [ ] I have added relevant documentation - [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR ### Code review Feel free to message or comment `@NVIDIA/mcore-oncall` to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged! All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft. #### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review" 1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**. 2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes. - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`. :warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing. Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled. #### Step 2: Final Review For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned. For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped. #### Step 3: Approved Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**. ### Merge Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

-import math

 import torch
 import torch.nn as nn
 import torch.nn.functional as F
@@ -40,7 +38,7 @@ def split_sinkhorn(
 ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
     """Split the mHC mapping and project ``comb`` to a doubly stochastic matrix."""
     pre, post, comb_logits = _split_mixes(mixes, hc_scale, hc_base, hc_mult)
-    return pre, post, fused_sinkhorn(comb_logits, iters, eps)
+    return pre + eps, post, fused_sinkhorn(comb_logits, iters, eps)
 
 
 class HyperConnection(nn.Module):
@@ -66,13 +64,12 @@ def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Te
             x = x.unsqueeze(2).expand(*x.shape[:2], self.hc_mult, x.size(-1))
         shape, dtype = x.shape, x.dtype
         xf = x.flatten(2)
-        rms_inv = 1.0 / (xf.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True) / math.sqrt(xf.shape[-1]) + self.eps)
+        rms_inv = torch.rsqrt(xf.square().mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + self.eps)
         mixes = F.linear(xf, self.fn.to(device=x.device, dtype=dtype)) * rms_inv
         pre, post, comb = split_sinkhorn(
             mixes, self.scale, self.base, self.hc_mult, self.sinkhorn_iters, self.eps
         )
-        # ``fused_h_aggregate`` is ``(x * h_pre.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=2)``, the same expression written here, so this is a kernel swap and not a
-        # change of formula -- unlike the Sinkhorn and compute_h helpers next to it, which differ from Core in their regularisation.
+        # ``fused_h_aggregate`` computes ``(x * h_pre.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=2)``.
         xs = xf.view(shape)
         y = fused_h_aggregate(xs, pre)
         return y.to(dtype), post, comb
@@ -82,7 +79,6 @@ def post(
         x: torch.Tensor, residual: torch.Tensor, post: torch.Tensor, comb: torch.Tensor
     ) -> torch.Tensor:
         dtype = x.dtype
-        # Core defines the mixing term as ``h_res.T @ residual`` while this module carries ``comb`` in the opposite orientation, so the
-        # transpose converts between the two conventions rather than being a layout tweak: passing ``comb`` unchanged silently computes a different residual mixing.
-        h_res = comb.to(dtype).transpose(-1, -2).contiguous()
+        # comb[source, destination]; the fused kernel already applies comb.T.
+        h_res = comb.to(dtype).contiguous()
         return fused_h_post_bda(h_res, residual.to(dtype), post.to(dtype), x, None)

@@ -3,8 +3,6 @@
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
-import math
-
 import pytest
 import torch
 import torch.nn.functional as F
@@ -247,6 +245,18 @@ def test_embedding_scatter_is_row_selective() -> None:
 S, B, N, C = 3, 2, 4, 16
 
 
+@pytest.mark.gpus(1)
+def test_split_sinkhorn_adds_epsilon_only_to_pre() -> None:
+    """Zero logits give pre=0.5+eps and post=1; amplify eps to catch omissions."""
+    mixes = torch.zeros(1, 1, (2 + N) * N, device="cuda")
+    scale = torch.ones(3, device="cuda")
+    base = torch.zeros((2 + N) * N, device="cuda")
+    eps = 1e-2
+    pre, post, _ = split_sinkhorn(mixes, scale, base, N, 3, eps)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(pre, torch.full_like(pre, 0.5 + eps), rtol=0, atol=1e-7)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(post, torch.ones_like(post), rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
 def _make_inputs(dtype: torch.dtype, device: str):
     """Build (x, residual, post, comb) with a real Sinkhorn-normalised ``comb``."""
     mixes = torch.randn(S, B, (2 + N) * N).to(device=device, dtype=dtype)
@@ -259,30 +269,30 @@ def _make_inputs(dtype: torch.dtype, device: str):
 
 
 def _reference_post(x, residual, post, comb):
-    """The pre-fusion expression, kept verbatim as the numerical contract."""
+    """DeepSeek stores comb[source, destination], so residual mixing uses comb.T."""
     dtype = x.dtype
     placed = post.to(dtype).unsqueeze(-1) * x.unsqueeze(-2)
-    mixed = torch.matmul(comb.to(dtype), residual.to(dtype))
+    mixed = torch.matmul(comb.to(dtype).transpose(-1, -2), residual.to(dtype))
     return placed + mixed
 
 
 @pytest.mark.gpus(1)
 def test_orientation_is_not_symmetric() -> None:
-    """Guard the guard: passing ``comb`` un-transposed must disagree."""
+    """Guard the fixture: comb @ residual must differ from comb.T @ residual."""
     _, residual, _, comb = _make_inputs(torch.float32, "cuda")
     assert not torch.allclose(comb, comb.transpose(-1, -2), rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3)
-    correct = torch.matmul(comb, residual)
-    swapped = torch.matmul(comb.transpose(-1, -2), residual)
+    correct = torch.matmul(comb.transpose(-1, -2), residual)
+    swapped = torch.matmul(comb, residual)
     assert not torch.allclose(correct, swapped, rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3)
 
 
 def _reference_forward(module: HyperConnection, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
-    """The pre-fusion aggregation, kept verbatim as the numerical contract."""
+    """Eager aggregation with epsilon inside the RMS square root."""
     if x.dim() == 3:
         x = x.unsqueeze(2).expand(*x.shape[:2], module.hc_mult, x.size(-1))
     shape, dtype = x.shape, x.dtype
     xf = x.flatten(2)
-    rms_inv = 1.0 / (xf.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True) / math.sqrt(xf.shape[-1]) + module.eps)
+    rms_inv = torch.rsqrt(xf.square().mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + module.eps)
     mixes = F.linear(xf, module.fn.to(device=x.device, dtype=dtype)) * rms_inv
     pre, _, _ = split_sinkhorn(
         mixes, module.scale, module.base, module.hc_mult, module.sinkhorn_iters, module.eps
@@ -301,13 +311,17 @@ def test_post_matches_pre_fusion_reference_bf16_gpu() -> None:
 
 
 @pytest.mark.gpus(1)
-def test_forward_aggregation_matches_pre_fusion_reference_gpu() -> None:
-    """Same, for the aggregation half: this is the only cover for the fused kernel."""
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("input_scale", [1.0, 1e-4])
+def test_forward_aggregation_matches_pre_fusion_reference_gpu(dtype, input_scale) -> None:
+    """Small activations expose epsilon placement; BF16 also covers FP32 parameters."""
     module = HyperConnection(hidden_size=C, hc_mult=N, sinkhorn_iters=3, eps=1e-6).cuda()
-    x = torch.randn(S, B, N, C, device="cuda")
+    x = torch.randn(S, B, N, C, device="cuda", dtype=dtype) * input_scale
     expected = _reference_forward(module, x)
     actual, _, _ = module(x)
-    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-4)
+    assert actual.dtype == dtype
+    tol = 2e-2 if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else 1e-4
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=tol, atol=tol * input_scale)
 
 
 _ROPE_KW = dict(config=None, use_yarn=False, device=torch.device("cpu"), dtype=torch.float32)
